key_insight: Learned diffusion proposals help constraint solving mainly when random multi-start is weak; otherwise, classical restart plus exact polishing often matches or beats them.
engineering_relevance: For continuous algebraic solvers, the biggest practical gain may come from smarter discrete repair/augmentation selection, while value proposals should be benchmarked against budget-matched random restarts.
method: Turn the constraint system into a factor graph and use a GNN diffusion denoiser to propose assignments.
Polish proposals with exact computer-algebra descent and verify them with a symbolic checker.
For augmentation selection, use a candidate-conditioned repair ranker over K options instead of exhaustive enumeration.
evidence_signal: Across synthetic families and eight real systems, learned proposals only beat random multi-start in a narrow high-dimensional regime; best-of-K random restart followed the exact curve 1-(1-q(n))^K with mean absolute error 0.012.
watch_item: Reported gains depend strongly on the problem regime, so fair evaluation must include the same refinement budget and a random multi-start control.
paper_title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems
